drhp.business: Capillary is a software product company offering AI-based cloud-native SaaS loyalty and engagement products (Loyalty+, Engage+, Insights+, Rewards+ and a Customer Data Platform) primarily to Enterprise Customers globally. It supports over 410 brands across 47 countries, enabling end-to-end loyalty programs, unified consumer views and cross-channel engagement.

concerns_observed: Company does not meet Regulation 6(1) SEBI ICDR profitability/net-tangible-asset eligibility; offer proceeds under Regulation 6(2) (loss-making FY23 and FY24)
High customer concentration - top 10 customers 55-59% of revenue; top 5 ~43% in FY25
Heavy dependence on a single unnamed third-party cloud provider (~45-56% of software/server charges) with rising multi-year annual spend commitments (USD 7.10m to 8.50m)
Large Offer-for-Sale component (up to 9,228,796 shares) from promoter CTIPL and investor Trudy Holdings; Company receives no OFS proceeds
Wide gap between promoter average acquisition cost (CTIPL Rs35.52, Aneesh Rs30.39) and recent transaction prices (3-year WACA Rs192.38; last-year WACA Rs486.36)
Foreign owned and controlled company; corporate-record traceability gaps and FEMA filing delays compounded with penalties

strengths_observed: End-to-end AI-led loyalty and engagement SaaS suite (Loyalty+, Engage+, Insights+, Rewards+, CDP) positioned by the issuer-commissioned Zinnov Report as a global leader by breadth of offerings
Global enterprise footprint - 410+ brands across 47 countries, 19 Global Fortune 500 customers, 16 offices
Strong revenue growth (FY23-FY25 revenue CAGR 53.06%) and turn to marginal profitability in FY25 after prior losses
High net revenue retention (112-143% across periods) and low churn (~6-10%), indicating durable enterprise relationships
Demonstrated acquisition-integration playbook (Persuade Group, Brierley+Partners, Tenerity Digital Connect) migrating acquired customers onto its cloud platform

sk.overview: Broadcasting and streaming is a segment of the global media & entertainment (M&E) industry undergoing a structural shift to a 'new video economy' - the transition from traditional cable/DTH to internet-delivered video (OTT, FAST, CTV). The shift is characterised by fragmentation of viewership, globalisation of content, and a move to ad-supported models, and it is driving M&E companies to adopt cloud-native, purpose-built streaming-video software for production, preparation, distribution and monetization.
